## MoodBuro 0.3.3

### Moodle view recovery

- When a Moodle page stops loading because the connection dropped, a request stalls for 30 seconds, or the page's web content process quits, MoodBuro checks that Moodle is reachable again and rebuilds the view on the page you were opening.
- Recovery only covers ordinary browsing (dashboard and course pages). Login, editing, quiz, submission and download pages are left alone, so no form is ever sent twice. If the same page stalls again right after a rebuild, MoodBuro opens the dashboard instead.
- During a longer outage MoodBuro keeps checking for about 15 minutes, then tells you that Moodle is still unreachable instead of giving up silently.
- If MoodBuro is in the background when Moodle comes back, the view is rebuilt as soon as you return to the window.
- MoodBuro checks your saved account before rebuilding, and rebuilds a site at most once every 90 seconds.

### Signing in during the Moodle cooldown

- While Moodle temporarily limits automatic sign-in, the toolbar now invites you to enter your password on the Moodle page instead of only waiting for the retry. Signing in yourself cancels the pending automatic retry.
- The message is shorter, keeps the organisation name readable in narrow windows, and shows in full in its tooltip.

### Install or upgrade

From MoodBuro 0.2.0 or later, check for updates in Settings → General. For a first installation or an earlier version, download the universal macOS DMG (Apple Silicon and Intel), verify it against `SHA256SUMS.txt`, quit MoodBuro, then drag the app into Applications.

The app is ad-hoc signed and not notarized. macOS may require first-launch approval in System Settings → Privacy & Security. macOS 12 is the configured minimum; full supported-platform, Intel runtime and installed update qualification remain in progress.

### Assets

- Universal `.dmg` installer
- Signed `.app.tar.gz` update archive and `.sig`
- `latest.json` stable update manifest for both Mac architectures
- `SHA256SUMS.txt`
